# Fund data

FundR uses Eastmoney's public fund directory and historical NAV feed. These
examples require an internet connection.

```{r fund-data, eval=FALSE}
funds <- FundR::fund_list()
head(funds)

nav <- FundR::fund_nav("000001", "2024-01-02", "2024-01-31")
head(nav)
```

Keep fund codes as character strings to preserve leading zeros. NAV rows are
sorted by date. The daily return is expressed as a percentage, so a value of
`1.25` means 1.25%. A successful query with no observations returns a zero-row
data frame. Money market yield series are outside the scope of `fund_nav()`.

# Example function

The package template includes `add_one()`, which adds one to a value.

<!-- 
This first section shows:

- the three parts necessary for a package: 'function', 'examples' and 'tests'.  
  + Note that the three following chunks have names accordingly.

-->

```{r function-add_one}
#' Add one to any value
#' 
#' @param value A numeric value
#'
#' @return Numeric. value + 1
#' @export

add_one <- function(value) {
  result <- value + 1
  return(result)
}
```

<!--
Here is an example on how to use the function.
This should be a reproducible and working example
-->

```{r examples-add_one}
add_one(12)
add_one(56)
```

<!--
Here are some unit tests to verify the function works as expected.
-->

```{r tests-add_one}
test_that("add_one works", {
  expect_equal(add_one(12), 13)
  expect_equal(add_one(56), 57)
})
```
